children: US gasoline futures rose above $3.30 per gallon, gaining for the second straight session, as a storm in the Gulf of Mexico threatened to disrupt refinery operations.
Refineries in US Gulf states account for about half of US refining capacity, which stands at 18.2 million barrels per day.
Meanwhile, continued attacks in the Middle East kept energy-market risks elevated despite improvement in regional shipments.
Russia’s ongoing restrictions on diesel exports and refinery disruptions, alongside China’s reported suspension of some October fuel exports, also tightened fuel markets.
Gasoline inventories were 7% below the five-year average as of September 25, according to the EIA, while refinery utilization stood at 92.5%.
The EIA also raised its 2026 and 2027 oil price forecasts, citing rapidly falling global inventories and supply risks.
Separately, the G7’s planned release of emergency crude and diesel reserves could provide some relief.

title: Gasoline Rises for Second Day
